checks: No eclipse at 13 of 33 covered epochs where the 1.43101 d period predicts one (each under half the typical depth, > 5 sigma below it). The period is probably wrong - the dips seen may be separate eclipses of a longer-period system.
writeup: TIC 437022904 is a candidate eclipsing binary star with an orbital period of 1.431008 days, detected through automated analysis of TESS photometry. The primary eclipse produces a dimming of 0.49%, while no secondary eclipse was detected. The eclipse signal achieves a detection significance of 573.0 in the Box-Least-Squares search, and pixel-level analysis confirms a peak signal-to-noise of 9.0, though the centroid offset of 2.9 arcsec from the target position warrants attention. The candidate does not appear in six major variable-star catalogs, making it a previously unlisted object. However, data quality checks reveal that alternating eclipses differ significantly in depth, suggesting the true orbital period is double the initial BLS detection - a pattern that affects interpretation of the eclipse properties but does not change the pixel-level confirmation or eclipse timing measurements.
